Score one skeletal branch

Source: R/mat.R
score_branch.Rd

The taper method uses explicit moving means of width three for both derivative stages; this replaces the upstream unspecified adaptive smoothing. Final scores use a width-three moving mean and power ten. Separation radii below one pixel are undefined and return NA.

Usage

score_branch(
  branch,
  property = c("parallelism", "separation", "mirror", "taper"),
  window = 5L,
  power = 10,
  estimator = c("mlv2023", "arclength"),
  reference_radius = 1,
  fit_tolerance = 1,
  units = c("pixels", "visual_degrees"),
  pixels_per_degree = NULL
)

Arguments

branch

A data frame/list with x, y and radius vectors.

property

Parallelism, separation, mirror or taper.

window

Local derivative integration half-window.

power

Final score exponent.

estimator

Published sample-based scores or physical arc-length scores.

reference_radius

Positive reference radius for new separation scores.

fit_tolerance

Positive geometric residual scale for new mirror scores.

units

Spatial units for the new estimator's window and references.

pixels_per_degree

Required calibration for visual-degree units.

Value

One numeric score per branch point.

Details

With `estimator="mlv2023"` this function returns the published values: points where the score is undefined (the two end points for parallelism and taper, whose window has zero width; every point of a branch with fewer than three points, or of a mirror branch with three or fewer) are scored 0, and that 0 enters the final moving mean, lowering the scores next to it. [compute_mat_properties()] under the default `branch_rule="invariant"` instead marks those points NA and averages only the defined values in each moving-mean window (NA where none is defined), so a branch end takes the value of its defined neighbour (before smoothing) and a branch too short for a property is NA, not 0. The default estimator also sums every window directly rather than as a difference of cumulative sums: the published form can round a radius pair (1, 1) to 0.99999999999999989 < 1 and so turn an exact separation of 0 into NA. A raw value of exactly 0 is a defined value in both modes; it is never replaced by NA, and smoothing averages it like any other value. Elsewhere the two modes agree up to rounding.

The arclength estimator integrates the piecewise-linear axis and radius exactly over clipped physical windows. Parallelism is axis arc length divided by the joint axis/radius arc length. Mirror is chord/arc straightness divided by one plus mean squared perpendicular error / fit_tolerance squared. Taper is consistency with the best affine radius, using a dimensionless RMS residual divided by window length. Separation is mean radius divided by (mean radius + reference_radius). The exponent applies afterward. These are versioned geometric descriptors, not claims of perceptual equivalence. A zero-length window is undefined (NA); inconsistent radii at duplicate points fail. The published estimator ignores none of these options: nondefault new unit/reference settings require explicit arclength selection.
